item.title: narratorAI
item.description:
## The Problem
Automated camera capture is easy; making sense of what was captured is not. This repo solves the narrow problem of turning periodic webcam snapshots into a spoken, character-voiced narration of whatever the camera sees. It is a demo of a three-stage pipeline: capture an image, describe it with a vision model, and read the description aloud with a synthetic voice.

item.title: Awesome AI Agents for Healthcare
item.description:
## The Problem
Agentic AI research in healthcare is published across venues and fragmented by modality (radiology, genomics, EHR), application (drug discovery, patient dialogue), and year. A clinician or researcher trying to track the field has no single index. This repo is that index: a curated, categorized list of papers, plus a survey paper and two data-visualization figures summarizing the literature landscape.

item.title: QloApps
item.description:
## The Problem
Small and mid-sized hotels need an online booking presence but face either expensive SaaS booking platforms with per-booking fees or generic CMS plugins that lack property-management features. QloApps addresses this by providing a free, self-hosted reservation system with a booking engine, property management, and a hotel website in one PHP application.

item.title: lemon chat
item.description:
## The Problem
Most chat tools route through a provider you don't control. This repo solves that with a self-hosted chat system—server you run yourself, client that works from a browser tab—where even the hosting admin can't read messages unless they belong to them. The README positions it as a Teamspeak/Mumble-style tool with end-to-end encryption layered on top of TLS.

item.title: whatseerr
item.description:
## The Problem
Self-hosted media request tools like Jellyseerr/Overseerr force users into a web UI. For households or communities where WhatsApp is the primary communication channel, that's a barrier — requests don't get made, or they get made through a middleman. Whatseerr bridges that gap by turning WhatsApp messages into Seerr API calls.

item.title: ekphos
item.description:

Researchers and writers who work in markdown need a tool that links notes, manages a knowledge graph, and supports vim-style editing without leaving the terminal. Obsidian does this in a GUI; Ekphos brings the same workflow to a TUI with a fraction of the resource footprint.

Ekphos is a Rust terminal application that renders markdown notes with an internal wiki-link graph, inline image support (iTerm2/Kitty/WezTerm/Sixel), vim modal editing, and themeable UI. ...

item.title: neural os
item.description:
## The Problem Training agents to interact with a real operating system is slow, serial, and hard to parallelize: every rollout needs a live desktop, and failures are expensive. NeuralOS replaces the OS with a neural model that predicts the next screen frame from mouse, click, and keyboard events, so policies can be trained and evaluated against a GPU-resident, differentiable environment instead of a physical machine.

item.title: liquid audio
item.description:
## The Problem
Real-time speech-to-speech AI requires a model that generates audio and text tokens with low latency, typically on resource-constrained devices. Most systems either stream text or audio separately, or rely on large backbones that cannot run interactively. Liquid Audio targets this gap with a lightweight end-to-end audio foundation model that interleaves text and audio token generation.
